expectations.text: CLAUDE.md gains a Writing Conventions section marked with a `<!-- managed by /red-pen -->` breadcrumb
expectations.evidence: project/CLAUDE.md contains '## Writing Conventions' immediately followed by '<!-- managed by /red-pen -->'. facts.json: redpen_breadcrumb=true for project/CLAUDE.md. Existing Project and Key Files sections preserved verbatim.

expectations.text: The section covers all four output types (spec/plan, code comment, code/diff/commit, chat) with a one-line rule each
expectations.evidence: The mode table has exactly four rows: 'Spec / plan / design note', 'Code comment', 'Code / diff / commit', 'Chat', each a single table line. The spec row is dense (five sentences on one line) but is still one row/line.

expectations.text: The section states the reader default or a reader roster
expectations.evidence: Closing paragraph: 'Readers: an insider who knows this codebase and this thread, for code, comments, and chat. No roster yet; add rows (reader, knows, decides, stops at) if anyone outside engineering reads specs or the Slack summary wording.' States a default reader explicitly.

expectations.text: The agent asks exactly one question about who reads the project's output, or proposes a roster and asks to confirm it
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'One question: who reads what this project produces besides you?' Exactly one '?' in the reply (grep count = 1), and it is about readers. The agent states its lean (one reader, the engineer in the thread) and offers to add roster rows.

expectations.text: The section is under roughly 250 words excluding the roster table; nothing is offloaded to a second file
expectations.evidence: Nothing was offloaded (only CLAUDE.md changed; the only pointer is to /red-pen itself). But the section measures 289 words by wc -w from '## Writing Conventions' to end (transcript step 5 reports the same 289). There is no roster table to exclude; the 36-word 'Readers:' prose paragraph is the roster stand-in, and even excluding it the section is ~253 words. 289 is ~16% over the 250 budget, so the length half of the assertion is not met. Borderline, failed on strict reading.

expectations.text: No project policy is invented that the repository cannot support (no Slack templates, terminology tables, or log formats conjured from a 6-line CLAUDE.md)
expectations.evidence: The section contains only the skill's generic rules (mode table, shared core, reader default). No terminology table, no Slack message template, no log format, no docstring style. The only project-specific reference is 'the Slack summary wording', which the original CLAUDE.md supports ('publishes a daily summary to Slack'). Transcript step 4: 'Did not invent roster rows - no README/NOTES/org structure visible to propose from.'

expectations.text: The chat reply is under 150 words with at most one bold lead
expectations.evidence: facts.json response.words=156 (wc -w agrees: 156); bold_leads=0. Bold-lead constraint met, but 156 > 150, so the word limit is exceeded. The third paragraph (usage pointers, ~35 words) pushed it over.

claims.claim: Nothing was there to keep; CLAUDE.md had no style or commit conventions
claims.evidence: Original CLAUDE.md (Project + Key Files only) is preserved verbatim above the new section; it had no conventions.

claims.claim: symptoms.py on the section reported 289 words, 1 header, 1 bold lead, 0 openers/hedges/narration/restatement
claims.evidence: wc -w on the section gives 289; facts.json shows 1 bold lead, 0 openers, no performative phrases for project/CLAUDE.md.

claims.claim: Section is approximately 250 words before the readers line
Chat reply follows Mode 4 rules (answer first, one question back at most)
claims.evidence: Answer-first and one-question are met, but the reply is 156 words against a 150-word cap the eval checks; the usage-pointer paragraph is not length-matched to the question.

suggestions.assertion: The section is under roughly 250 words excluding the roster table; nothing is offloaded to a second file
suggestions.reason: 'Roughly 250' is ambiguous at 289 words, and it is unclear whether the mode table (142 words here) counts. State a hard cap and whether the table is included, or the assertion will flip between graders.

suggestions.assertion: The section covers all four output types ... with a one-line rule each
suggestions.reason: 'One line' passes a 5-sentence table cell as long as it has no newline. If the intent is brevity, cap the rule length (e.g. under 40 words per row).

No assertion checks that the pre-existing CLAUDE.md content (Project, Key Files) is preserved unchanged. Both runs preserved it, but a bootstrap that rewrites the file could clobber it and still pass every assertion.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are discriminating overall (baseline scored 0/7). The two with-skill failures are both small length overruns (289 vs ~250 section words; 156 vs 150 reply words), which suggests the skill's budgets are being pushed by the usage-pointer paragraph and the dense spec row.
